content.title: A Tree, for the World; for the Akhirah
content.subtitle: How Islam Honors Tree Planting as Sadaqah Jariyah
content.body:
Every year, nearly three times more trees are cut down than are planted!

Tell me, how long does it take to cut down a fully grown tree? One hour? Two hours? Three hours? Yet it takes nature years to fill that empty space.

Every year, the world loses nearly 15 billion trees. In contrast, only about 5 billion new trees are planted. That means the world has a net loss of nearly 10 billion trees every year.

This is not just the loss of a few trees. Along with them disappear the habitats of countless creatures, biodiversity declines, the carbon burden in the atmosphere increases, and our future becomes even more uncertain.

The tree we cut down today may be the shade the next generation will never have.

Tree Planting: A Means of Sadaqah Jariyah

Islam does not limit caring for creation to worldly benefit alone. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Whenever a Muslim plants a tree or grows a crop, and a bird, a person, or an animal eats from it, it is counted as charity for him."

— Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith: 2320

In another hadith, he gave even more glad tidings:

"Whenever a Muslim plants a tree, whatever is eaten from it, stolen from it, or consumed by birds or animals is counted as charity for him."

— Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 1552

Even at the moment the Hour begins, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ emphasized the importance of planting trees. He said,

"If the Hour is established while one of you has a sapling in his hand, and he is able to plant it before it is established, then let him plant it."

— Musnad Ahmad, Hadith: 12902

A Tree, for the World; for the Hereafter

Protecting the greenery around us is not merely an environmental responsibility. For a Muslim, it can be an act of worship, an act of charity, and a beautiful means of Sadaqah Jariyah.

June-July are considered the most suitable months for tree planting. So, this rainy season, let us plant at least one tree. If planting a tree yourself isn’t possible, you can take part in tree-planting through a trusted organization. As-Sunnah Foundation distributes a large number of trees every year. You can also participate in this form of Sadaqah Jariyah by supporting tree-planting initiatives through such organizations.

The tree you plant today may one day provide shade for a weary traveler, shelter for a bird, or fruit for someone who is hungry. And for every benefit it brings, rewards may continue to be quietly added to your record of good deeds, InshaAllah.
